nodes.What it is: A gripper is the tool at the end of an arm. Parallel jaws pinch, suction uses a pressure difference, and soft fingers bend around objects.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Match geometry and material to objects before adding learning; no universal gripper handles every surface. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: MIT manipulation course; industrial gripper designers
nodes._accessibility_reason: Choosing and testing fingertips is approachable; suction plumbing and soft fabrication add work. Accessibility refers to the simulated/offline entry point; real hardware may take months.

nodes.What it is: Contact forces and friction determine whether an object slips. Form closure blocks motion geometrically; force closure uses frictional contacts to resist disturbances.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Friction models help explain failures but uncertain surface properties limit predictions on hardware. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: Lynch and Park; MIT Robot Locomotion Group
nodes._accessibility_reason: A small simulated contact example needs no electronics. Accessibility refers to the simulated/offline entry point; real hardware may take months.

nodes.What it is: A pick-and-place system finds an object, chooses a grasp, moves the arm, and releases it at a destination. Each stage must use consistent coordinates and recover when a grasp fails.
nodes.Prerequisites: Coordinate frames; basic inverse kinematics; gripper safety
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Reliable recovery and repeatable evaluation matter more than a single successful video. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: A fixed scene and simulator let software students get an early win. Accessibility refers to the simulated/offline entry point; real hardware may take months.

nodes.What it is: Teleoperation lets a person move an arm through a leader arm or another input device. Recording camera images and joint motion produces examples for imitation learning.
nodes.Prerequisites: Joint limits; calibration; timestamps; emergency stop
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Dataset quality, synchronized cameras and operator ergonomics constrain useful demonstrations; ALOHA 2 improves collection hardware. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Documented leader-follower assembly is accessible, but calibration and wiring still require care. Accessibility refers to the simulated/offline entry point; real hardware may take months.

nodes.What it is: A grasp detector predicts where a gripper could hold an object from an image or point cloud. A good grasp score does not guarantee the arm can reach it without collisions.
nodes.Prerequisites: Point clouds; camera calibration; grasp mechanics
nodes.Frontier state 2026: GraspNet supplies a benchmark and Contact-GraspNet predicts 6D grasps; clutter, sensor gaps and execution remain limitations. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Public data makes offline experiments practical before hardware integration. Accessibility refers to the simulated/offline entry point; real hardware may take months.

nodes.What it is: Pose estimation finds an object position and orientation relative to a camera. The robot transforms that estimate into its own coordinates to approach the object.
nodes.Prerequisites: Rigid transforms; camera intrinsics; RGB-D data
nodes.Frontier state 2026: FoundationPose supports pose estimation and tracking; symmetry, occlusion and calibration still complicate grasp execution. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Recorded RGB-D sequences support a software-first demo; hardware needs careful calibration. Accessibility refers to the simulated/offline entry point; real hardware may take months.
